programmes.d: Johnny isn't interested in what Charles Grodin has to say, but you might be. B.B. King and Amy Yasbeck also grace the couch.
John Candy stops by with screen icon Maureen O'Hara. Plus, Jim Valvano appears and Johnny gives up smoking in the monologue.
The first lady of TV, Betty White, critiques Johnny's sketch comedy performance, and quizzes him on the wonders of nature.
Stand-up master Super Dave Osborne sends up President George Bush, VP Dan Quayle and....reggae music!
Comedian David Brenner says people will like stuff when it's offered for free. Also discusses his life in New York City and his Italian identity. Claims not to have enjoyed E.T.

Rich Hall details his comedy climb: wrote for David Letterman, quit to write "Not Necessarily the News" and then joined Saturday Night Live. He shows Johnny the mini spa he made, for dolls, in his bathroom.
Stand up genius David Brenner jokes about music from India, chewing gum with liquid centers, and his favorite restaurant: The International House of Pancakes.
Johnny jokes about President Reagan and Boy George in the monologue; plus, Rich Hall, Robert Black and Richard Guindon head to the couch.
David Brenner, Roger Rees and child actor Miko Hughes join Johnny and Ed for another episode full of laughs.
In his very first appearance on The Tonight Show, Robin admits he was a geeky kid, discusses herpes and cocaine, and makes fun of Ronald and Nancy Reagan.
Comic great and sometimes skier Jerry Seinfeld talks about keeping warm on the slopes and decorating his living room with mirrors. Also appearing on this episode is Dallas star Victoria Principal.
Comic/actor Paul Reiser says that material goods are more important than health, and British actress Lynn Redgrave comments on Margaret Thatcher and the Falklands war.
Robin discusses the cancellation of his hit TV series Mork and Mindy, and his new movie, The World According to Garp.
Catch Bill Maher's first appearance on The Tonight Show. He dishes on President Reagan and VP George Bush. Neil Simon and Joe Garagiola also appear.
In his first appearance on the show, Jim Carrey impersonates Elvis, Jack Nicholson, E. T. and all of the Muppets. Also visiting Johnny are Robert Blake and Bud Greenspan.
Comic Howie Mandel incites hilarity discussing his wife, his family and his upcoming birthday. Also guesting are actress Mimi Kennedy and humorist Calvin Trillin.
SNL star Kevin Nealon tells a story about getting a live lobster and setting it free Ð in a forest. Charles Grodin and Linda Thorsen are also on the show.
Full House dad Bob Saget explains his attempts at trying to improve his appearance. He also comments on the various people he meets at his gym.
Stand-up comic Bill Maher describes growing up half Jewish and half Catholic. Actor James Woods talks about his recent wedding at the Graystone Mansion in Beverly Hills.
TV star and stand-up comic Paul Reiser tells Johnny what he says to people, so they'll think he's listening to them when he really isn't.
Roseanne star Tom Arnold chats about his nervousness to be on the show. His wife and co-star Roseanne Barr also appears and they talk about their marriage and kids.
Comic genius Robin Williams rips into Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas, and teams up with comedian Jonathan Winters for a hysterical dog and cat routine.
Author and comedian Jeff Foxworthy chats about his bestselling book, 'You Might be a Redneck if.' Also on the show is Dallas star Patrick Duffy.
Comedian and actor Drew Carey talks about cold weather and global warming. Fellow guests are David Steinberg and Regis Philbin.
Comedian Keenan Ivory Wayans recalls how his first appearance on the show, in 1986, was the highlight of his career.
Comedy Stars Jerry Seinfeld and Charles Grodin share loads of laughs over eyeglasses, doctor visits, and (wait for it) bowling shoes.
Is the cost of a night at the movies getting you down? Jerry SeinfeldÕs got a hilarious rant. Actress Lynn Redgrave fills us in on playing Cleopatra.
When was your last laugh over pay phones or tux rentals? Jerry Seinfeld catches you up, and comedian Martin Mull shows off his cat and dog paintings.
